harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built and verified the replicated CORP.EXAMPLE Samba AD environment. Both controller-outage scenarios passed, and all services are restored and healthy.
actions_performed: Provisioned node1 and joined node2 as replicated AD controllers.
Joined node3 as the member file server and node4 as the client.
Bound directory, DNS, Kerberos, and SMB services to the 10.100.79.0/24 identity network.
Created engineering and infrasetuser, then published the writable engineering share with the required welcome file.
Stored the generated user credentials in /root/corp-user.env on node4 as root:root mode 0600.
Tested each controller outage independently, including fresh Kerberos authentication, DNS, machine trust, and SMB write/read/delete operations.
Restored both controllers and removed temporary duplicate credential files while preserving the required node4 environment file.

evidence.summary: Node1 provisioned CORP.EXAMPLE, node2 joined as a DC, and both final controller checks report active AD roles, both DC DNS records, healthy DRS, replicated member/client computer objects, and identity-only core listeners.
The enabled user was added to engineering on node1; node2 received the objects through replication and issued the user a TGT and LDAP ticket.

evidence.requirement: Joined member server, engineering share, permissions, and welcome.txt
evidence.summary: Node3 reports a healthy join and trust, active smbd/winbind, root:engineering mode 2770 share ownership, exact infraset-samba content, group-restricted write configuration, and SMB bound only to 10.100.79.12. Node4 successfully read and wrote through the share.

evidence.requirement: Joined client and protected credential file
evidence.summary: Node4 reports Join is OK and healthy trust. The required SAMBA_USER and nonempty SAMBA_PASSWORD keys remain in /root/corp-user.env as root:root mode 0600; auxiliary credential copies were removed.

Controllers and file server use enp8s0 on 10.100.79.10–12 with no core service binding on management addresses. Node4 routes share traffic over enp8s0 from 10.100.79.13 and uses both identity-network DNS servers.

evidence.requirement: Authentication, DNS, and share access with node1 down
evidence.summary: After a healthy baseline, node1 was stopped and its identity listeners disappeared. Node2 remained active; node3/node4 selected it, node4 obtained a fresh TGT directly from 10.100.79.11 and completed a new SMB write/read/delete. Node1 was restored and both DRS views recovered.

evidence.requirement: Authentication, DNS, and share access with node2 down
evidence.summary: Node2 was stopped after a healthy baseline and its identity listeners disappeared. Node1 remained active; node3/node4 selected it, node4 obtained a fresh TGT directly from 10.100.79.10 and completed a new SMB write/read/delete. Node2 was restarted, became fully ready with zero database errors, and both DRS views returned to healthy.

attempts.error: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired at 2026-09-01T18:17:18.348000+00:00

diagnosis.summary: The proximate failure was lease expiration, not a proven final configuration defect. Direct evidence shows a working node3 domain trust/share, correct welcome.txt, protected node4 credentials, and authenticated SMB read/write. However, the structured report was never returned, and the selected records do not independently prove DC replication, node4 machine join, AD group membership, all-node identity-network binding, or failover in either direction; those appear only in executor-authored summaries referencing omitted commands.

evidence.finding: The cluster expired at 18:17:18 UTC. The last direct successful checks finished at 18:16:30 and 18:16:34—only 44 seconds before expiration.
There were 118 terminal commands and 372,468 tokens. Several transport-level “completed” records actually had nonzero return codes, so that label does not mean shell success.
Provisioning first failed because samba-ad-provision was missing, then failed again because the requested 2016 functional level exceeded this Samba build's supported 2008 R2 DC level.

DC2 obtained a Kerberos TGT and LDAP service ticket, but its join failed with NT_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER; smbclient also reported that /etc/samba/smb.conf could not be loaded. Similar ticket-only SMB tests on node4 failed.

Stopping DC1 produced systemd state “failed” rather than the script's expected “inactive.” The subsequent node3 DC-selection test exceeded the 120-second tool timeout. Later successful failover is asserted only by summaries whose underlying records were omitted.

Node4 successfully read welcome.txt and created/deleted a file over authenticated SMB; /root/corp-user.env was root:root mode 0600. Node3 showed /srv/corp/engineering as root:engineering mode 2770, welcome.txt with exact content infraset-samba, active smbd/winbind, and “Join is OK.”

No selected successful command directly shows DC2's final role, DRS health, node4's machine trust, engineering membership, or fresh-credential SMB access during each controller outage. Full completion is therefore not independently established.

likely_causes.cause: Deadline management: configuration and verification continued into the final minute, leaving no safe interval for structured submission before lease expiration.
Missing package/version preflight caused destructive provisioning retries and avoidable recovery work.
Samba configuration and credential invocation were not stabilized early; missing smb.conf and conflicting ticket-only/-N usage caused repeated join and SMB failures.
Failover validation was brittle and insufficiently bounded: it required one exact systemd state and allowed wbinfo calls to hang beyond the tool timeout.
Late, unsuccessful password-rotation attempts consumed scarce time despite an already usable credential.

next_attempt_guidance: Preflight immediately: install samba-ad-provision and all DC/member/client packages, inspect supported functional levels, and omit --function-level=2016 because the task does not require it.

Discover the actual identity interface on every fresh node; do not assume enp8s0. Configure persistent addressing, hostnames, Samba interfaces, routes, and resolvers containing both DC identity-network addresses.
Work in gates: provision DC1 and test DNS/Kerberos; join DC2 and prove bidirectional DRS; create the final user/group; join node3 and node4; publish and test the share; only then run failover tests.

Create valid krb5.conf, resolver configuration, and smb.conf before Samba joins or client commands. Avoid -N when Samba needs a password; separately verify kinit/service tickets and a known-good password-authenticated SMB flow.
Generate the user's final password once, use it when creating the AD account, and install the same shell-safe value in /root/corp-user.env as root:root 0600. Avoid late password rotation.

For each controller outage, destroy cached user tickets, stop one DC, prove its identity listeners are absent, obtain a new ticket through the survivor, resolve DNS, perform a new SMB write/delete, and test machine trust. Restore it and verify DRS before testing the other DC.
Treat any non-active systemd state as an outage only after listener checks. Wrap wbinfo and similar probes in short per-call timeouts plus a bounded overall retry loop.
Capture direct acceptance evidence after each gate and reserve several minutes for the final structured report; stop optional remediation once all requirements have passed.
